topic.name: Calculating Derivatives From Data and Tables

question.text:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

\[ f(2)=1, \quad f'(2)=\dfrac{1}{2}, \quad g(2)=6, \quad g'(2)=3 \]

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)$ at $x=2.$
question.explanation:
Using the quotient rule, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right) = \dfrac{f'(x)g(x)-f(x)g'(x)}{(g(x))^2}. \]

At the point where $x=2$, this gives

\begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)\right|_{x=2}&=\dfrac{f'(2)g(2)-f(2)g'(2)}{g^2(2)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 6 - 1 \cdot 3}{6^2}\\[5pt] &=0. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Derivative of a Quotient Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=2$ are given in the table below.

$x$ $f(x)$ $g(x)$ $f'(x)$ $g'(x)$
$2$ $4$ $3$ $5$ $1$

If $h(x) = \left( f(x)+1 \right) \left( 2g(x)-2 \right),$ compute $h'(2).$
question.explanation:
The product rule states that \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big(uv\Big) = u \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} +v \dfrac{\textrm du}{\textrm d x}. \]

Let $u=f(x)+1$ and $v=2g(x)-2.$ Differentiating each, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = f'(x) \qquad \text{and}\qquad \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} = 2g'(x). \]

Substituting this into the product rule gives

\begin{align*} h'(x) &=u \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} +v \dfrac{\textrm du}{\textrm d x}\\[5pt] &=\left( f(x)+1 \right) \cdot 2g'(x) +\left( 2g(x)-2 \right) \cdot f'(x) \\[5pt] &=2g'(x)\left( f(x)+1 \right) + 2f'(x)\left( g(x)-1 \right). \end{align*}

At $x=2$, this gives

\begin{align} h'(2) &=2g'(2)\left( f(2)+1 \right) + 2f'(2)\left( g(2)-1 \right)\\[5pt] &=2\cdot 1\cdot (4+1)+2\cdot 5\cdot (3-1)\\[5pt] &=2 \cdot 5 + 10\cdot 2\\[5pt] &=30. \end{align}

example.title: Computing the Derivative of the Product or Quotient of a Composition of Functions Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
For the functions $v(x)$ and $w(x),$ you're given the following data:

\[ v(2)=-3, \quad v'(2)=1, \quad w(2)=-2, \quad w'(2)=-4 \]

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( v(x) - 2w(x) \big)$ at $x=2.$
question.explanation:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( v(x) - 2w(x) \big) = v'(x) - 2w'(x). \]

At the point where $x=2$, this gives

\begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( v(x) - 2w(x) \big)\right|_{x=2} &= v'(2) - 2w'(2) \\[5pt] &= 1 - 2\cdot (-4) \\[5pt] &= 1 + 8 \\[5pt] &= 9. \end{align*}
